title: PRAgent: AI-Assisted Physics Paper Reproduction
subtitle: Capabilities and Evidence from a 100-Paper Project
comments: Technical report, 12 pages, 5 main figures and a supplementary cohort figure. Code and public research artifacts: https://github.com/xi-zhao/RunThePaper
abstract: PRAgent connects physics-paper interpretation, numerical implementation and scientific assessment in a human-guided research workflow. We examine the system through public implementations and a documentary audit of a fixed 100-paper project. Three cases provide concrete evidence: resource-bound code that refines large integer decisions with 60-digit arithmetic; quantum dynamics implemented in conserved particle sectors; and finite-ensemble discord calculations that expose a discrepancy with an analytical reference. A surface-code case illustrates a system-level distinction: checks pass for an implemented repetition-code proxy, while the original paper target remains unaccepted. To evaluate the breadth of these results, we trace 3,241 archived result-object records from 95 papers to their declared comparison conditions and references, and reconcile summary and detailed assessment records. This audit finds that the 26 papers with all associated checks historically labelled reproduced and the 26 with summary-level review marked passed are disjoint. Consequently, check-label fractions cannot serve as a scientific reproduction rate. The contribution is an inspectable implementation and assessment workflow, supported by numerical examples and explicit evidence links. The archive establishes bounded capabilities within that workflow; it does not yet establish an autonomous-agent success rate or complete reproduction of the cohort.
